mentions.name: Vizzly
mentions.description: A visual testing and review tool that makes visual quality part of the development workflow rather than an after-the-fact testing phase. It offers a local TDD CLI (vizzly tdd) for iterating on UI changes instantly against real screenshots, accepts screenshots from existing infrastructure (Playwright, Puppeteer, BrowserStack, CI runners), and builds a per-commit visual review dashboard with position-based comments, review rules, and deep links. The CLI/SDK are open and the local TDD features can be used without the hosted service, with the goal of closing the developer-designer gap.
mentions.problem: Most visual testing tools spin up a recreated environment (copy the DOM + assets, render in their own infra) and compare diffs, so what they check isn't what users actually see, forcing developers to debug rendering quirks in someone else's browser; visual quality is also usually an after-the-fact testing phase instead of part of the dev workflow.
mentions.audience: focusing on developer workflows first; asks for feedback from folks who've wrestled with visual diffs
mentions.source_excerpt: I’ve been working on [Vizzly](https://vizzly.dev) -- my attempt to make visual quality part of the development workflow, not an after-the-fact testing phase.
